I’m afraid I don’t have a way to pull “votes” directly from http://digdeep.io—or from its underlying infrastructure—because: 1. **No Public API** – There’s no publicly documented endpoint that exposes vote counts keyed to an IP address. 2. **Privacy & Security** – Even if there were such data, exposing it would raise serious privacy issues. Most sites keep per‑IP voting records private so users can’t game the system. 3. **Technical Limits** – As a text‑based assistant without network access, I can’t run live queries against external servers or databases. ### What You Can Do Yourself | Step | How | |------|-----| | **Find the server’s IP** | Use `nslookup`, `dig`, or online services:
`$ dig +short digdeep.io`
or
`$ host digdeep.io`. | | **Check public analytics** | Some sites publish aggregate stats (total votes, top contributors) on their dashboard or through APIs. Look at `/api/votes/summary` or similar endpoints if they exist. | | **Contact the admins** | Reach out to the website owners or support team asking whether they expose per‑IP vote metrics. | | **Inspect your own logs** | If you’re running a service that tracks votes, look into your backend logs/database where each vote record should include the originating IP. | If you’re looking for *your* own IP address when visiting the site, simply open a browser console and type: ```javascript fetch('https://api.ipify.org/?format=json') .then(r=>r.json()) .then(console.log); ``` That will return something like `{ ip: "203.0.113.42" }`. --- Let me know if you’d like more detailed instructions on any of those steps!
